target_customer: Startups and scaleups in Brazil and Latin America (retail, fintech, SaaS, marketplaces) that pay for AI and human customer support
problem: Companies in Brazil handle most customer service on WhatsApp and need cheap, scalable support; Cloud Humans provides an AI agent (claudIA) plus an omnichannel platform with human fallback.
business_model: Usage based pricing per ticket answered plus platform fees

founders.name: Ian Kraskoff
prior_employers: Uber Eats Brazil (launcher, left as GM)
founders.background_notes: YC page: former door to door salesperson and product launcher for unbanked customers in the Americas.

founders.name: Bruno Cecatto
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only a quote.

founders.name: Felipe Serra de Oliveira
founders.background_notes: YC page: expanded Uber Eats across 30 cities in Brazil.

technical_complexity.rationale: Chatbot and ticket automation integrated with customer systems; later GPT based agent is engineering over foundation models.

defensibility.rationale: Integration with customer back office systems helps, but customer support AI is widely copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The company publishes comparison pages against Zendesk, Movidesk and Octadesk (undated); no acquisition of Cloud Humans found.

market_need_then: WhatsApp is the main customer service channel in Brazil per the company's own comparison page and demand for outsourced support from startups was served by a human agent marketplace in 2021.

brand_strength.rationale: Branded agent persona claudIA is a plus, but the company name is generic and no independent press on the brand was found.

pivots.from: On demand marketplace of human customer service and sales professionals
pivots.to: AI agent claudIA with human fallback
pivots.why: Not stated in sources opened; a 2021 seed article describes the earlier human marketplace model

outcome_analysis: Cloud Humans started in 2020 as a way to connect companies to remote support professionals, raised a seed led by Canary in March 2021, and shifted to an AI agent, claudIA, with a team of 30. Total funding is small and sources conflict, and no exit or shutdown was found. The pivot to AI support is the main story; whether it found strong product market fit is not shown by independent sources.
notes: Seed round of R$6.3 million led by Canary is reported by Startupi and Seedtable (search results; the Startupi page was not opened due to fetch limits). The amount is stated in reais, so amount_usd is null; Seedtable shows about 1.1M USD, an aggregator conversion. Totals conflict: CB Insights 1.53M, Fundediq 6.2M across 7 rounds with a May 2025 seed, Prospeo 250K. None verified. Competitors named by the company's own pages are undated, so the as-of list is empty. The YC page lists New York while other sources say Sao Paulo.
